newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel, jet trade at firmer level.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel, jet trade at firmer level.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel traded higher on Wednesday along with stronger swaps and crude values, traders said.
Gas oil was traded for the first time in two weeks when a European major sold 150,000 barrels to a Chinese trader at $20.60 per barrel for July 31-August 4 lifting, free-on-board (fob) basis.
The same two parties traded a similar gas oil parcel on July 2 at $163 per tonne ($21.87 per barrel).
The traded level on Wednesday was 10 cents higher than the lowest offer on Tuesday and indicated a recovery from the three-year low levels of $19.80 per barrel offered last week.
Swaps for August gained 15 cents per barrel to be last quoted at $21.35/$21.45, while September rose 25 cents to be indicated at $22.35/$22.55.
Traders were mixed on market direction.
While some said the firmer swaps levels did not reflect a true picture of bearish physical fundamentals with China remaining absent, others were seeing some light at the end of the tunnel.

Despite talk that the diesel flow to South America has ended with the three cargoes sold to Argentina and Paraguay, a trader with a major said the Latin America region remained keen to seek cheap and available oil may it be from the MidEast, Mediterranean or East Asia.
Even Brazil, who normally uses its own tankers to ship cargoes, might be in the market for cheap oil outside their normal sources.

Traders said since the demand-supply position in the Middle East is balanced, buyers from Latin America might be more interested to obtain readily available diesel from refineries in Singapore or South Korea.
They said MidEast suppliers are committed to meeting higher demand from East Africa, and premiums there are now indicated at 30-40 cents per barrel above MidEast quotes, fob basis.
Qatar was said to have recently sold a cargo at a 30-cent premium fob.
Floating prices in Singapore however remained stuck in a 40-to-50-cent discount range to Singapore spot quotes, fob, but one major limited the discount to 20 cents.
Nepal's tender to buy 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil for August attracted low bids from a European major for the first cargo lifting 11-20 at $162.69 per tonne, cost-and-freight (c+f) Madras/Haldia.
The second cargo for August 21-31 lifting saw a low offer from a Mediterranean trader at $163.44 per tonne, c+f basis.

An industry source said state-owned Indian Oil Corp would soon start talks with Middle Eastern producers for its annual term import contracts for gas oil and kerosene, kicking off with Kuwait Petroleum Corp at the end of this month.
IOC was not expected to raise its term import volumes with each of the producers--Kuwait, Abu Dhabi and Bahrain.
Jet fuel was also traded higher with a European major selling 100,000 barrels to a Singapore trader at $23.50 per barrel for August 5-9 lifting, fob.
Traders said the buyer could be pricing its sales to Indonesia.
Jet fuel was last traded on July 9 at $22.10 for July 24-28 lifting fob between a US trader to a Singapore trader.
Traders said jet fuel values were currently overpriced in light of weak regional demand.
With the physical sales of jet fuel and gas oil on Wednesday the spread between the two products widened to $2.90 per barrel, which is an anomaly from the swaps prompt regrade of $1.80/$2.00.
The swaps regrade had corrected itself after the physical deals and was lower earlier in the day at $1.60/$1.80.
